# detect


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

The Learn page has one box to start something new. You paste a link, a
paper, a topic, a file name or some text. As you type, one quiet line
says what abhyasa will do. When two readings are both likely, the box
asks one short question. Options show only when they change the result.

[`detect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#detect)
makes this reading from the text only. It makes no network call and it
resolves no host name. The one lookup is a match against the titles of
your vault documents, and the caller does that lookup
([`vault_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#vault_title)).

A goal can name its sources: a folder on this Mac, a GitHub repo, or a
folder that is in your vault.
[`named_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#named_sources)
finds them by name. The caller reads the folder names from the disk one
time
([`folder_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#folder_names)),
and [`detect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#detect)
only looks them up, so it still makes no network call and reads no disk.

Import the link rules of `sources`, so the box and a walk from a link
agree on what a paper and a local address are.

## The words

Each reading has one quiet line. The numbers in the lines come from the
settings, so a line is never false.

## Folding a name

A title matches when it is the same text with case and marks folded, so
`Maghā` finds `magha`. Only case and marks fold: `nakṣatras` does not
find `Nakshatras`. This is the fold of the concepts list.

## One source

[`source_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#source_of)
reads one word as a source: a paper, a GitHub repository, a docs site, a
video, a local link or a folder. A word with no shape of a source gives
None. A bare `github.com/...`, a name with a dot and a slash, or a host
with a known ending such as `example.com`, gets `https://`. The video
hosts are the video hosts of `research.SOCIAL`. A folder is a path that
starts with `/` or `~`, or a folder name in `folders`. A bare
`owner/name`, such as `fastai/diffusion-nbs`, is a GitHub repository.

### as_url

``` python
def as_url(
    s:str
)->str | None:
```

*`s` as a web link: as it is, with `https://` for a bare link, or None.*

A word with no shape of a source, such as a topic, gives None.
[`local_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#local_name)
resolves no name, so `printer.local` is local with no lookup.

``` python
test_eq(source_of('github.com/a/b'), ('repo', 'https://github.com/a/b'))
test_eq(source_of('arxiv:1706.03762'), ('paper', '1706.03762'))
test_eq(source_of('~/code/course22')[0], 'folder')
test_eq(source_of('course22', folders=('course22',))[0], 'folder')
test_eq(source_of('http://printer.local/')[0], 'local')
test_eq(source_of('attention'), None)
test_eq(source_of('example.com'), ('site', 'https://example.com'))
test_eq(source_of('node.js'), None)
test_eq(source_of('fastai/diffusion-nbs'), ('repo', 'https://github.com/fastai/diffusion-nbs'))
test_eq(source_of('and/or'), None)
```

## Named sources

[`folder_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#folder_names)
reads the folder names under the source folders (the setting
`sources.roots`), `depth` levels down. It leaves out dot folders and the
build folders of `SKIP_DIRS`. It folds each name, so `Course22` finds
`course22`. Two folders can have the same name, so each name gives a
list of paths. This is the one part that reads the disk. The app does it
one time and keeps the result.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/detect.py#L81"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### folder_names

``` python
def folder_names(
    roots, depth:int=2
)->dict:
```

*Each folder name under
[`roots`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/settings.html#roots),
folded, to its paths: `depth` levels down, with no dot folder and no
`SKIP_DIRS` folder.*

A small tree: two folders named `notes` at two depths, a dot folder, and
a folder three levels down that is too deep.

``` python
import tempfile
```

``` python
top = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
for d in ('course22/nbs/deep', 'other/Notes', 'notes', '.hidden/x', 'proj/node_modules'): (top/d).mkdir(parents=True)
fn = folder_names([top, top/'not-there'])
test_eq(sorted(fn), ['course22', 'nbs', 'notes', 'other', 'proj'])
test_eq(len(fn['notes']), 2)
```

[`named_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#named_sources)
finds the sources that a text names. It gets the folder names and the
roots in the vault. It makes no network call, and it reads the disk only
to find a path with spaces. Each source is a chip, with:

- `kind`: `folder`, `repo`, `gh`, `doc` or `link`;
- `name`, `path`, `count` (the documents in the vault, when it knows),
  and `filed` (it is in your vault already);
- `id`: what the Start form sends: `vault:<root>`, `folder:<path>`,
  `repo:<path>`, `gh:<owner>/<name>`, `doc:<doc_id>` or `link:<url>`.

A root that is in the vault wins over a folder on the disk with the same
name. A name of a common folder, such as `src` or `data`, is never a
source: a goal uses these words for other things. A document title
matches only as a whole phrase of at least 6 characters, with a space or
a sign in it, so a one-word title does not match a plain word.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

```

Two folders with the same name give two chips, each with its path. A
common folder name gives none.

``` python
cs = named_sources('Use notes and data, and fastai/fastcore', names=fn)
test_eq([c.id for c in cs], ['folder:' + str(p) for p in fn['notes']] + ['gh:fastai/fastcore'])
test_eq(named_sources('Use fastai/fastcore', roots_in_vault={'fastai/fastcore': 9})[0], _chip('folder', 'fastai/fastcore', count=9, filed=True, id='vault:fastai/fastcore'))
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources('Read Attention Is All You Need first', {'Attention Is All You Need': 'd1', 'Attention': 'd2'})], ['doc:d1'])
```

Two paths in one paste give two chips. A space, a new line or a comma
can come between them. A path can have spaces in its name: put it in
quotes, or paste it as it is when the folder is on the disk. Then the
longest part that is on the disk is the path. This is the one check of
the disk in
[`named_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#named_sources).

``` python
a, b = top/'course22', top/'other'
for sep in (' ', '\n', ', ', ','): test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(f'{a}{sep}{b}')], [f'folder:{a}', f'folder:{b}'])
```

A folder with a space in its name stays one chip, alone or before
another path. A quoted path is one chip, also when it is not on the
disk.

``` python
sp = top/'My notes'; sp.mkdir()
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(str(sp))], [f'folder:{sp}'])
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(f'{sp} {a}')], [f'folder:{sp}', f'folder:{a}'])
test_eq([c.id for c in named_sources(f'"{top}/Not here yet" {a}')], [f'folder:{top}/Not here yet', f'folder:{a}'])
```

[`on_disk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#on_disk)
is the disk part, for the caller: a folder chip with a `.git` folder is
a local repo (`repo:<path>`), and a folder that abhyasa does not file
gets `why`, from
[`folder_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#folder_why).
It does not run `git`: a repo on the disk is text that abhyasa does not
trust.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/detect.py#L156"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

test_eq(on_disk(named_sources('/tmp/no-such-folder-x'))[0].why, 'abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')
```

## The reading

[`detect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#detect)
gives an `AttrDict`:

- `kind`: one of
  `empty paper repo site doc topic text ask video local folder sources goal file_name`.
- `line`: the quiet line.
- `ask`: None, or the question, with two answers as (label, kind), and
  `doc`: the id of the vault document, when it names one.
- `options`: the fields that matter, from
  `pages tool title subject find`.
- `send`: the fields of `/walk/new` for this reading.
- `sources`: for `sources`, each source as (kind, link or path).
- `chips`: the sources that the text names
  ([`named_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#named_sources)).
  Start files each one that is not in the vault.

A **goal** is one line of 7 to 60 words with “I want”, “I would like”,
“help me”, “teach me”, “how do I” or “how to”, or a line that names a
found source. A **folder** is a path. `counts` holds what the caller
found on the disk for a path: `notebooks`, `files`, `repo`, or `why` it
is refused. The folder then asks: “Walk through it” or “Use it for a
goal”.
[`names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/ground.html#names),
`roots_in_vault` and `docs` (a dict of title to id) go to
[`named_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#named_sources).

[`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/model.html#pick) is the
answer to a question: `doc`, `topic` or `text`. `file` is the name of a
dropped file: a `.pdf` is in the vault as the document `doc`, and a
`.md` or `.txt` is in the box as text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/detect.py#L201"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

    doc:str='', names:dict=None, roots_in_vault:tuple=(), counts:dict=None, docs:dict=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*What abhyasa does with `text` from the Start box. `titles`: vault
titles to match, or a dict of title to document id; `folders`: folder
names that you named.*

## The cases

`DETECT_CASES` holds each shape that the box knows, with the kind it
must give. The tests of the app use the same table.

Each case gives its kind.

``` python
for t, ti, k in DETECT_CASES: test_eq(detect(t, ti).kind, k)
```

A vault title asks first. Its first answer walks through the document,
and the answer `doc` sends its title as `ref`.

``` python
r = detect('Nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',))
test_eq(r.ask.a, ('Walk through that document', 'doc'))
test_eq(r.ask.q, 'Nakshatras is in your vault.')
test_eq(detect('nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',), pick='doc').send, dict(ref='Nakshatras'))
test_eq(detect('Nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',), pick='topic').kind, 'topic')
test_eq(detect('nakshatras', {'Nakshatras': 'd1'}).ask.doc, 'd1')   # with a dict, the question carries the document id
test_eq(detect('nakshatras', {'Nakshatras': 'd1'}, pick='doc', doc='d1').send, dict(ref='d1'))
```

With research off, the topic line says that the tutor uses its own
knowledge.

``` python
assert 'own knowledge' in detect('how attention works', research=False).line
test_eq(detect('how attention works').send, dict(topic='how attention works'))
```

Pasted text shows Title, Subject and Find concepts only. A sentence of 7
to 12 words answered as a text is one line of text.

``` python
test_eq(detect('a\nb').options, ('title', 'subject', 'find'))
test_eq(detect('a\nb').line, 'Pasted text, 2 lines. abhyasa finds the ideas in it and makes a walk.')
test_eq(detect('The moon spends about one day in each of the lunar mansions.', pick='text').kind, 'text')
```

A repo ticks the tool box. A site says how many pages it reads. A paper
says how many ideas a walk has at most.

``` python
r = detect('github.com/vedicreader/fossick')
test_eq((r.options, r.send), (('tool',), dict(url='https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick', tool='on')))
test_eq(detect('https://docs.python.org/3/', pages=5).line, 'A docs site. abhyasa reads the pages in this folder. It reads at most 5 pages.')
test_eq(detect('1706.03762').line, 'An arXiv paper. abhyasa reads it in full and makes a walk of up to 12 ideas.')
test_eq(detect('arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762').send, dict(url='https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762'))
```

A file name is never a topic: it is the vault document of that name, or
a hint to drop the file. A dropped file is certain: the box never asks
for it.

``` python
test_eq(detect('Nakshatras', ('Nakshatras',), file='naks.pdf').line, 'A PDF. abhyasa reads it in full.')
test_eq(detect('My paper', file='My paper.pdf', doc='d7').send, dict(ref='d7'))
r = detect('Line one.\nLine two.', file='notes.md')
test_eq((r.kind, r.line, r.options, r.send['title']), ('text', 'A text file. abhyasa finds the ideas in it.', ('title', 'subject'), 'notes'))
```

Several sources at once give each source, and one chip for each. A
folder name that you named is a folder.

``` python
r = detect('github.com/a/b, ~/code/fastbook')
test_eq(r.sources, (('repo', 'https://github.com/a/b'), ('folder', '~/code/fastbook')))
test_eq(r.send['sources'], ['gh:a/b', 'folder:' + str(Path('~/code/fastbook').expanduser())])
test_eq(detect('course22', folders=('course22',)).kind, 'folder')
r = detect('~/code/course22p2\n~/code/fastbook')
test_eq((r.line, [c.name for c in r.chips]), (LINES['sources'].format(n=2), ['course22p2', 'fastbook']))
```

A goal names its sources. Here the folder names come from a fake disk,
and `course22p2` is in the vault. The chips are a folder on the disk, a
folder in the vault and a GitHub repo.

``` python
names = {'course22': [Path('~/code/personal/orgs/course22').expanduser()], 'fastbook': [Path('/h/o/fastbook')]}
r = detect(GOAL, names=names, roots_in_vault=['course22p2'])
test_eq(sorted(c.id for c in r.chips), sorted(['folder:' + str(names['course22'][0]), 'folder:/h/o/fastbook', 'gh:fastai/diffusion-nbs', 'vault:course22p2']))
assert 'reads the sources below first' in r.line
test_eq(r.send['goal'], GOAL)
```

With research off, the goal line says that ideas with no passage keep
the tutor’s words. A goal that names no source says that abhyasa looks
on the web.

``` python
assert "keep the tutor's words" in detect(GOAL, research=False).line
test_eq(detect('help me learn how attention works in a transformer').line, LINES['goal_alone'])
```

A folder with its count from the disk asks what to do. `pick='walk'`
sends the folder. A refused folder says why.

``` python
p = str(Path('~/code/x').expanduser())
r = detect('~/code/x', counts={p: dict(notebooks=44, files=50)})
test_eq((r.line, r.ask.a, r.ask.b, r.ask.chip), ('A folder with 44 notebooks. abhyasa files them in your vault.', ('Walk through it', 'walk'), ('Use it for a goal', 'goal'), f'folder:{p}'))
test_eq(detect('~/code/x', counts={p: dict(notebooks=0, files=1, repo=True)}, pick='walk').send, dict(sources=[f'repo:{p}']))
test_eq(detect('/tmp/x', counts={'/tmp/x': dict(why='abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')}).line, 'abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')
test_eq(detect('course22', names=names).chips[0].path, str(names['course22'][0]))
```

## The vault title

[`vault_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#vault_title)
finds the one document on the main shelf whose title is the text, with
case and marks folded, and gives its title and its id. It skips your
walks, talks and concepts. A text of more than 6 words never matches.
The box asks after each pause in your typing, so the folded titles are
kept in an index. One small query checks if the vault changed (its count
of documents, the time of the newest, and the length of all titles);
only then is the index made again.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/detect.py#L270"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

`q`, or `q` with no file ending, folded; None when there is none.*

A test vault with one document named Nakshatras. A part of the title
does not match. A new document shows at once.

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
d = lr.vault.add('Some text about nakshatras.', title='Nakshatras', source='test://n')
test_eq(vault_title(lr.vault, ' NAKSHATRAS '), ('Nakshatras', d['doc_id']))
test_eq(vault_title(lr.vault, 'naksha'), None)
lr.vault.add('Some text about rasis.', title='Rasis', source='test://r')
test_eq(vault_title(lr.vault, 'rasis.pdf')[0], 'Rasis')
```
